draft.title: Energy efficiency
card: Useful energy is the energy that does the job we want. A light globe is meant to give light, so the light is its useful energy.
Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in. It can be written as a fraction or a percentage. A device that turns 100 J into 25 J of useful energy is 25% efficient.
The rest of the energy is wasted. It is not destroyed, but it ends up as a form we did not want, often heat or sound.
An old globe gives off a lot of its energy as heat, so it is less efficient. An LED light wastes less as heat, so it is more efficient.
draft.remember: Efficiency is useful energy out divided by total energy in. The rest is wasted, often as heat or sound.

a.q: A toy motor takes in 50 J of energy. It gives out 30 J as movement, which is the useful energy. What is its efficiency?
a.why: Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in = 30 ÷ 50 = 0.6, or 60%. The 40% option is the share that was wasted, not the share that was useful.
a.clue: Divide the useful energy by the energy put in.

b.q: Priya compares two lamps in her room. Both take in 20 J of energy each second. Lamp A gives 4 J of light and lamp B gives 10 J of light. Which statement is correct?
opts: Lamp B is more efficient, as it wastes less energy
Lamp A is more efficient, as it wastes less energy
Lamp B is more efficient, as it takes in more energy
Lamp A is more efficient, as it gives out less heat
b.why: Lamp B is 10 ÷ 20 = 50% efficient and lamp A is 4 ÷ 20 = 20% efficient. Lamp B turns more of its input into light, so it wastes less. Both lamps take in the same energy, so the input does not make B more efficient.
b.clue: Both lamps take in the same energy, so compare the useful light.

b.best: Lamp B is more efficient, as it wastes less energy
